paper_title: Homomorphism-Distinguishing Closedness for Graphs of Bounded Tree-Width
classifications: Theory of computation → Graph algorithms analysis
statement: Still, Conjecture 1 remains wide open. As an intermediate step, it may be interesting to consider minor- and union-closed classes of bounded tree-width. More precisely, let F be a graph class closed under taking disjoint unions and minors, and there is some k ≥ 1 such that every F ∈ F has tree-width at most k. Can we show that F is homomorphism-distinguishing closed? Towards this end, it may also be interesting to obtain a direct proof of Corollary 13 that does not rely on the characterization from Theorem 10.
context: We proved that for every k ≥ 1 the class Tk of all graphs of tree-width at most k is homomorphism-distinguishing closed. As a consequence, we could answer an open question from [1] and precisely classify the subgraph counts detected by k-WL. Still, Conjecture 1 remains wide open. Can we show that F is homomorphism-distinguishing closed?
